ing: half chopped for the marinade, half finely diced for serving
st: Soak the guajillo chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the achiote paste, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, [[2 tsp]] salt, half the onion and [[0.5 cup]] of the pineapple until smooth.
Toss the sliced pork with the marinade in a bowl or zip bag. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over high heat with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Cook the pork in batches for 3 minutes per side until browned at the edges and cooked through to 145°F (63°C). Do not crowd the pan.
Add the pineapple slices to the pan and sear for 2 minutes until charred, then chop them.
Chop the pork into small pieces and mix with the chopped pineapple.
Warm the tortillas on a dry hot pan for 30 seconds per side.
Fill each tortilla with pork, the remaining diced pineapple, diced onion and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
Put the chicken in a pot with [[2 cups]] of the broth, half the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer covered for 35 minutes until cooked to 165°F (74°C). Remove the chicken and keep the broth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] lard in a skillet. Toast the chiles for about 20 seconds per side until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
In the same skillet, fry the almonds, raisins, tortilla, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns for 3 minutes until toasted, then add the sesame seeds for 30 seconds.
Char the tomatoes, remaining onion and garlic in a dry pan for 8 minutes until browned.
Drain the chiles. Blend them with the toasted mixture, the tomatoes, onion, garlic and [[1 cup]] of the broth until smooth, adding more broth as needed.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] lard in a large pot. Pour in the paste carefully, since it will spatter, and fry for 8 minutes, stirring often.
Add the chocolate, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 cup]] more broth. Simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring, until dark and thick like gravy.
Add the chicken to the mole and simmer for 10 minutes to warm through. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice and tortillas.
Mix the onion, chile, half the cilantro and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl. Mash with a fork to release the flavor.
Cut the avocados in half, remove the pits and scoop the flesh into the bowl.
Add the lime juice, which stops the avocado from browning.
Mash with a fork to the texture you like, leaving it a bit chunky.
Fold in the diced tomato and the rest of the cilantro.
Taste and add more salt or lime. Serve right away with tortilla chips.
Heat the broiler. Place the tomatillos and chiles on a baking sheet.
Broil for 5 minutes until blistered and charred, then flip and broil 4 minutes more.
Let them cool a few minutes, then add everything including any juices to a blender.
Add the garlic, onion, cilantro, lime juice and [[0.75 tsp]] salt.
Blend until mostly smooth, adding water a spoonful at a time to loosen it.
Taste and adjust salt and lime. Serve cold or warm with chips, tacos or enchiladas.

ing: half quartered, half finely diced to serve
st: Put the pork, quartered onion, [[4 cloves]] garlic, [[2 tsp]] salt and the water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Lower the heat, cover partly and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the pork is tender.
Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the chiles with the remaining garlic and [[1 cup]] of the cooking broth until smooth. Strain it into the pot.
Add the hominy and oregano. Simmer for 30 minutes more so the flavors blend.
Remove the pork, shred it into bite-size pieces and return it to the pot. Taste and adjust salt.
Ladle into bowls. Top with cabbage, diced onion, radishes and a squeeze of lime.
Char the poblanos under a hot broiler or over a gas flame for 10 minutes, turning, until blackened all over.
Put them in a bowl, cover with a plate and let them steam for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins.
Cut a slit in each pepper, remove the seeds and stuff in a stick of cheese. Dust lightly with flour.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, broth and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer in a pan for 10 minutes until slightly thick.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold in the yolks and [[0.5 tsp]] salt gently.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each pepper in flour, then coat in the egg mixture. Fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with the warm tomato sauce spooned over.

ing: finely diced, plus extra for topping
st: Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the chiles with the tomatoes, garlic, broth and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth. Strain.
Simmer the sauce in a saucepan for 10 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Warm the oil in a skillet. Dip each tortilla in the oil for 10 seconds per side to soften, then dip it in the sauce.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, a little cheese and onion, then roll up and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and cover with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes until bubbling. Drizzle with crema and scatter with onion before serving.
Simmer the pork with [[6 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and half the garlic for 1 hour 15 minutes until very tender. Shred the meat.
Soak the corn husks in hot water for 30 minutes until pliable. Soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the remaining garlic, cumin and [[1 cup]] of the broth, then cook the sauce 5 minutes with the shredded pork.
Beat the lard with an electric mixer for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Mix the masa harina, baking powder and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Beat into the lard, alternating with [[2.5 cups]] broth, until it is like thick cake batter.
Spread about [[0.25 cup]] masa over the smooth side of a husk, leaving a border. Spoon pork filling down the middle.
Fold the sides in and then fold up the bottom. Stand the tamales open-end up in a steamer basket.
Steam over simmering water, covered, for 1 hour. Add water as needed.
Rest for 15 minutes before unwrapping. The masa should pull cleanly away from the husk.

ing: thinly sliced, pickled with lime to serve
st: Blend the achiote paste, orange juice, lime juice, garlic, vinegar, oregano, cumin and [[2 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Toss the pork with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). If using banana leaves, warm them over a flame for a few seconds to soften them.
Line a baking dish with the leaves or foil. Add the pork and marinade and wrap tightly to seal.
Roast for 3 hours until the pork shreds easily with a fork and reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Meanwhile, slice the onion thin and soak in lime juice and a pinch of salt for 30 minutes to quick-pickle.
Shred the pork in its juices.
Serve on warm tortillas topped with the pickled onion.

ing: cut in wedges, or 6 oz tortilla chips
half roughly chopped, half sliced thin to serve
st: Fry the tortilla wedges in [[0.5 cup]] hot oil in batches for 2 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels and salt lightly.
Blend the tomatoes, chiles, garlic, chopped onion, broth and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wide skillet. Pour in the sauce and simmer for 8 minutes until it thickens a little.
Add the chips to the sauce and toss for 1 minute so they soften slightly but still have some bite.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan in the rest of the oil until the whites are set.
Divide the chilaquiles between plates. Top with the eggs, cheese, crema and sliced onion. Eat right away.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Brush the corn with the melted butter if using.
Grill the corn for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until tender with charred spots.
Spread each hot ear with an even coat of mayonnaise.
Roll or sprinkle the corn with the cotija so it sticks all over.
Dust with chile powder and a pinch of salt. Serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

ing: for rolling, plus 1 tbsp for the dough
st: Bring the water, butter, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the salt to a rolling boil in a saucepan.
Take the pan off the heat. Add all the flour at once and stir hard until a smooth dough forms.
Return to low heat and stir for 1 minute to dry out the dough, then cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time until the dough is smooth and glossy.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star tip.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] sugar and the cinnamon on a plate.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Pipe 5-inch strips into the oil, cutting with scissors. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain briefly, then roll in the cinnamon sugar while hot. Serve warm.
